title: Bohr's Postulates — Concise Statement and Meaning
topicTitle: Postulates of Bohr's atomic model and its application
notes: The four postulates, stated cleanly with the physical meaning of each — the fastest way to secure full marks on the 'state the postulates' question. Derivations and applications are in the main note and the companion application tab.

The electron in a hydrogen atom revolves only in certain fixed circular orbits around the nucleus. While in such an orbit it does **not** emit or absorb energy, although it is accelerating. Each orbit is a *stationary state* with a definite energy. Meaning: this postulate suspends classical electrodynamics inside the atom.

Only those orbits are permitted for which the angular momentum is an integral multiple of h/2π: $mvr=\frac{nh}{2\pi}$, n = 1, 2, 3, … The integer n is the principal quantum number. Meaning: the allowed orbits are discrete because the angular momentum comes in packets of ħ.

Energy is emitted or absorbed only when the electron jumps between orbits: $h\nu=E_{2}-E_{1}$ (emission when it falls to a lower level, absorption when it is raised). Meaning: this is exactly Planck's quantum hypothesis applied to atoms, and it is what produces sharp spectral lines.

The Coulomb attraction of the nucleus provides the centripetal force for the circular motion: $\frac{mv^{2}}{r}=\frac{kZe^{2}}{r^{2}}$. Meaning: the mechanics is classical; only the *allowed states* are quantum — a hybrid (semi-classical) model.

Ground state: lowest energy orbit (n = 1). Excited state: any higher orbit. Ionisation: complete removal of the electron (n = ∞). Binding energy: −Eₙ, the energy holding the electron. All definitions follow directly from the postulates.
confusion: ❌ Stationary orbit means the electron is at rest. ✅ It revolves, but the orbit is stationary *in energy* (non-radiating).
❌ Bohr's postulates were derived from classical mechanics. ✅ They were imposed; only the force condition is classical.
❌ The frequency condition applies to the electron's own motion. ✅ It concerns the emitted/absorbed photon only.

universalFacts: Bohr's model was published in 1913 — one year after Bohr joined Rutherford in Manchester.
The postulates apply strictly to one-electron species: H, He⁺, Li²⁺, Be³⁺.
Postulate 2 was later *derived* by de Broglie (standing matter waves) — turning an assumption into a consequence.
examples: **Problem:** Why do the postulates make the atom stable? **Solution:** in a stationary orbit (postulate 1) the electron accelerates without radiating, so it neither loses energy nor spirals in — stability is postulated, not explained classically.

summary: Bohr's model rests on four postulates: (1) the electron in hydrogen revolves only in certain fixed circular orbits of definite energy and neither emits nor absorbs energy while in one; (2) only orbits with angular momentum mvr = nh/2π are permitted, n = 1, 2, 3, …; (3) energy is emitted or absorbed only during a jump between orbits, hν = E₂ − E₁; (4) the Coulomb attraction provides the centripetal force, mv²/r = kZe²/r². Postulate 1 suspends classical electrodynamics inside the atom, postulate 2 makes the allowed orbits discrete, postulate 3 is Planck's quantum hypothesis applied to atoms, and postulate 4 keeps the mechanics classical — which is why the model is called semi-classical. The vocabulary of the model follows directly: ground state (n = 1), excited state (any higher orbit), ionisation (n = ∞) and binding energy (−Eₙ).
importantConcepts: Postulate 1 — stationary orbits of definite energy in which the electron does not radiate
Postulate 2 — quantisation of angular momentum, mvr = nh/2π, n = 1, 2, 3, …
Postulate 3 — frequency condition, hν = E₂ − E₁, applied only to emitted or absorbed photons
Postulate 4 — force condition, mv²/r = kZe²/r², the classical Coulomb balance
Model vocabulary: ground state, excited state, ionisation (n = ∞) and binding energy −Eₙ
importantStatements: A stationary orbit means constant energy, not rest: the electron revolves but does not radiate.
The postulates were imposed, not derived; only the force condition is classical mechanics.
Postulate 2 plus postulate 4 together fix the orbit radii; without postulate 2 a continuum of orbits would be allowed.
The frequency condition concerns the emitted or absorbed photon, not the electron's own motion.
The postulates apply strictly to one-electron species: H, He⁺, Li²⁺, Be³⁺.

keyPoints: Postulate 1 → stability; postulate 3 → sharp spectral lines.
mvr = nh/2π means angular momentum arrives in packets of ħ.
hν = E₂ − E₁ is Planck's relation applied to an atomic transition.
The model is semi-classical: quantum states, classical motion.
specialNotes: The postulates were published in 1913, one year after Bohr joined Rutherford in Manchester.
Postulate 2 was later derived by de Broglie from standing matter waves, turning an assumption into a consequence.
Stationary orbits are not orbitals: Bohr's orbits are fixed 2D paths of definite radius.

Attach one clause of meaning to each postulate; bare statements lose half the marks.
Say 'one-electron species' when quoting applicability — it is the commonest precision slip.
